featured_reviews.name: Ayush G
featured_reviews.review_text:
A Seafood Disaster – Masooli Restaurant

Visited Masooli expecting good seafood. What we got was very disappointing.

We ordered crab garlic, surmai garlic masala, bombil thecha fry, surmai green masala, rice with plain fish curry, solkadi and lime soda. The only real savior in the entire meal was the surmai green masala. The solkadi and lime soda were fine.

Everything else was a letdown. The fish curry had no tanginess, no salt, no flavour. It tasted flat and unfinished. For a seafood restaurant, getting a basic fish curry wrong is shocking. The crab garlic and bombil thecha fry were also disappointing.

I even called the waiter and asked him to taste the fish curry himself. He did not argue or defend it. He was so sure I was right that he did not even attempt to try it.

Service was good and the waiter was polite and attentive. But good service cannot save bad food.

Prices are high, but the taste does not justify it at all. Very disappointing experience. Would not return.

featured_reviews.name: Nameeta Chikhalkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
I visited Masoli recently and honestly, the experience was very disappointing. The service was pathetic — no staff attended to us until we had to repeatedly ask, even for basic things like water. Drinks were served late, and overall, there was no attentiveness at all.

The food was another letdown. We ordered Pomfret Fry which was undercooked, with most of the flesh still raw. The Bombil Thali was completely bland — the javla had no taste and no salt (even after adding salt, it was flavorless). The kolambi masala was extremely spicy but without any real taste or balance, and I usually have a high spice tolerance. On top of that, the bhakri served was not rice bhakri but maida, chewy and totally off.

Special mention to the staff handling our table, Manish — he was not attentive at all and definitely needs to be trained in customer service. If customers are paying their hard-earned money, the least expected is basic hospitality and properly cooked food.

Overall, a very poor experience.
Not at all worthy to visit there are many more place which u people can try it worthless

featured_reviews.name: Padam Bhushan
featured_reviews.review_text: I went to this eatery on a friend's recommendation. It's a modest space with cosily placed tables. The ambiance and maintenance are typical of a mid-range restaurant. The food is really fresh and tasty, though I had to limit myself to a few options because the most of food items are from Konkani cuisine, which is very hot and spicy. Whatever I ate was delicious, and they deserve full marks for it. However, the prices of each item are rather high, making my total experience less enjoyable. I would recommend this restaurant, but only if you are willing to pay exorbitant rates!

featured_reviews.name: Vinayak Thakur
featured_reviews.review_text: After long time, we enjoyd delicious non veg food. Maasoli is situated in Dadar West opp. Veena world office. featured_reviews.name: sonia mehta
featured_reviews.review_text:
It’s been a while since we’ve enjoyed an authentic Maharashtrian meal! At first glance the place makes your feel right at home, very true to its name! We had such a great meal on Sunday, we were three of us - my brother, my sister and I.
The best thing to do when you visit is let the owner suggest their specials for you to eat, we didn’t even open the menu - we tried the Chonak Fry - 10/10, we tried the Bombil fry- 12/10 ( the filling inside the Bombil blew our mind, we had the Alu Wadi with Prawns filling - 10/10!
For main course we had the Amti with Rice Bhakri and Ravas Fry ( the Ravas so incredibly fresh) the main course was 10/10 and to top it off we also tried their Prawns Bhaat / Pulav - it was so damn good! 100/10….the Sol Kadis we tasted took us back home honestly. After this meal all we needed was our bed to sleep on cause we were in a complete food coma. An absolutely outstanding meal with a very comfortable seating and ambiance! A definite must visit again and again!

featured_reviews.name: Naresh Shirodkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Fish Curry Rice is a true celebration of coastal flavours and seafood mastery. Their seafood spread is outstanding — the surmai and pomfret are impeccably fresh, the halwa and bombil melt beautifully, and the fish fry along with the prawns curry are rich, fragrant, and deeply satisfying.

What truly stole the show were the tisrya sukka, mori masala, and kalva sukka — bold, soulful preparations that burst with authentic coastal character. The must-try list is long for a reason: prawns aluwadi, stuffed pomfret, bombil thecha fry, and chounak fry are each crafted with precision and irresistible flavour.

Their thalis deserve special praise — generous, well-balanced, and layered with flavour, offering a complete journey through coastal cuisine. A special mention to owner Sandesh Bhat — the heart and soul of FCR — who ensures taste and consistency are always bang on, and who, along with his attentive team, is always on his toes with spot-on recommendations tailored to your mood and palate.

A place where freshness meets finesse, and every plate tells a story of spice, sea, and tradition.

featured_reviews.name: KPExplorer
featured_reviews.review_text: This resturant in primiraly from Pune which is only one in Mumbai Dadar kohinoor is was way beyond expectations .. good try for fish lovers, with great service from staff to decently priced thalis. They start with timbal a kokum drink as apetiser. Their fish curry is very delicious with perfect taste. They also serve senior citizen thali at 450 in which they gave 2 fish fry. Crab thali was also great. Their Ghavna with curry is an amazing combination

featured_reviews.name: guptepooja
featured_reviews.review_text:
Excellent place and way better than the Pune branch. It's open from 11.30am to 11pm...so you get served even at 5pm

They cook fresh stuff so order may take time but it's fresh! Amazing taste and super fresh fish. Blessed to have this joint in Dadar which works as a perfect combination of fresh seafood+ authentic goan cuisine+ economical.  We ordered mutton + pomfret fry thali and chicken thali. Fish was super duper fresh. My 6yrs old child finished the meals with no left over food in her plate; which itself is a big compliment.

Soham manages this really well. He also gifted a small soft toy fish to my child for new years.

Let the photos do the justice.

featured_reviews.name: Sunit Katkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Saw a lot of food vloggers show this place. Big mistake of believing them. Only good thing is the welcome drink called Tival. The prawns sukka was more curry and rubber like prawns. Only slightly better dish was crab masala. Sol kadhi had no kick. Maybe Gajalee and Sindhudurg have spoilt me by giving very good Sol Kadhi. We asked for Rice Bhakri expecting it to be soft like other places. This felt like it was cooked a day before and just reheated and served. It was too hard to be called a rice Bhakri.

Regret not going to Dutta Boarding House in Parel or even Gomantak next door. Had crab masala last week at Dutta Boarding.. FCR does not have that zing but it's better than the rubber prawn sukka taste.

Sorry, will not believe food vloggers from now on.

customer_updates.text:
The restaurant serves authentic Maharashtrian cuisine, and it was an outstanding experience. We started with Agri Matka and Chulivarcha Chicken, both of which were bursting with flavor. The Agri Matka had that traditional rustic touch, slow-cooked to perfection, while the Chulivarcha Chicken, prepared on a traditional clay stove, was smoky, tender, and incredibly delicious.

For starters, we tried the Prawn Sukka, which was a perfect blend of spices, with succulent prawns cooked in a dry, aromatic masala. It was the ideal start to the meal. We also couldn't resist the Prawn Biryani, which was fragrant and loaded with juicy prawns. The balance of spices and flavors in every dish was just spot on.
Overall, this restaurant is a must-visit for anyone craving authentic Maharashtrian food. Every dish was prepared with care, and the flavors stayed true to the region's culinary heritage. I can't wait to go back and try more!

featured_reviews.name: H Nanda
featured_reviews.review_text:
Located in Dadar, on the busy gokhale road, this non veg restaurant is known for sea food.  Restaurant is clean and well maintained.   Service is also clean and neat.  While sea food is good, chicken items are quite ordinary ( tried chicken biryani, butter chicken - nothing great).  On the other hand prawn dishes were good.  Food preparation is Maharashtrian flavor.   Prices are reasonable.
Peak times and peak days would have some wait time to get the table.  Parking is a major problem,  though they have valet service board, I do know where are going to park your vehicle.   Nearest known parking is near Shivaji Park or Kohinoor mall ( BMC  Parking), both about a kilometer away.  I have had food here about five to six times.  Worth a try.

featured_reviews.name: chinu's kitchen
featured_reviews.review_text:
I visited The Big Fish & Co. on 4th January while I was shopping around Dadar with my mom and sister. While shopping nearby, we asked a local person for a good restaurant recommendation, and she suggested this place — and honestly, it turned out to be a great choice.
Right from the entrance, the experience was pleasant. The security guard at the door was very polite and kind. He asked if we had a reservation (we didn’t), but luckily a few tables were available. Since we were just three people, we were seated comfortably without any wait.
The ambience is quite good — warm, comfortable, and very suitable for families and friends. There were absolutely no negative points when it came to the atmosphere. What really touched my heart was the attentiveness of the staff. They listened carefully, were patient, and ensured everything was smooth. The service was quick, with no unnecessary delays, which I truly appreciated.
Coming to the food — it felt very local and authentic, something I personally connect with. The dishes were unique and well-prepared. We ordered tandoori prawns, which were medium-sized and nicely cooked. I also ordered a thali and a crab dish, both of which were absolutely delicious and the dessert tooo it’s new for me being a konkani
Overall, it was worth the visit. Great food, warm service, and a lovely atmosphere. I truly loved the experience and would definitely recommend this place.

featured_reviews.name: Paurnima Patil
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Coast & Bloom at Dadar and it turned out to be a truly memorable dining experience that beautifully celebrates coastal and regional Indian flavors with a refined touch.

We began with the Lobster Thermidor, which was served in a rich, creamy mushroom sauce accompanied by sautéed vegetables, bread, and a perfectly cooked egg. The dish was indulgent, flavorful, and luxuriously satisfying. Alongside, we had the Tandoori Prawns, which carried an excellent smoky char from the tandoor. Paired with fresh green chutney and a sweet-tangy mango pickle, the combination elevated the entire starter experience.

For the main course, we opted for the Malvani Fish Curry with Ravas. The fish was exceptionally fresh, tender, and cooked to perfection, soaking beautifully in the aromatic Malvani gravy. We also tried the Chettinad Chicken, which had a bold, spicy profile and was packed with deep, authentic flavors.

To complement the curries, we had Malabar Parotta, Ghavane, and Chilli Cheese Garlic Naan. Each bread brought a different texture and paired wonderfully with the gravies, with the ghavane being a particularly delightful and unique accompaniment.

featured_reviews.name: Alok Shettigar
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re a seafood lover looking for authentic Mangalorean-style delicacies in Mumbai, Sion Lunch Home is the place to be. Located just a five-minute walk from Sion railway station, this eatery has been my go-to spot for the past two years, and I can confidently say it never disappoints.

Ambience & Seating

The place is clean and well-maintained, but it doesn’t have a very large seating capacity. Whether you opt for the AC or non-AC section, expect a waiting time—sometimes as long as 40 minutes to an hour. Due to its immense popularity, the restaurant does not accept reservations, so it’s always bustling with seafood enthusiasts.

Food & Specialties

The main reason for the crowd? The exceptional seafood, prepared in true Mangalorean style. I highly recommend trying their fish thalis and fish fries, which are consistently fresh and flavorful.

Must-Try Dishes:

Prawns Fry – Crispy, well-spiced, and utterly delicious.

Squid Fry – Perfectly cooked and packed with coastal flavors.

Bombil Fry – A Mumbai favorite that’s crispy on the outside, soft inside.

Pomfret Thali – A full-fledged meal featuring succulent pomfret fish.

Surmai Thali – A classic favorite for those who love kingfish.

Neer Dosa – Light, fluffy and an excellent companion to their flavorful gravies.

Mutton Sukka – My personal favorite; the spice blend is simply spot-on.

Fish Platters: A Family Favorite

If you’re visiting with family, the fish platters are a must-try. They offer a great variety and are perfect for sharing, ensuring you get to taste a bit of everything.

Final Verdict

Despite the long waiting time, the experience at Sion Lunch Home is always worth it. The food quality, authentic preparation, and reasonable prices make it one of the best places in Mumbai for seafood lovers. If you enjoy coastal cuisine, this spot should be at the top of your list!

featured_reviews.name: Chef Vaidehi Pathare
featured_reviews.review_text:
I had heard a lot about Gomantak in Dadar. On my recent visit, I finally decided to try it. It was raining heavily that day. Even then, the restaurant was completely packed. They have both AC and non-AC sections. I had to wait for about 15 to 20 minutes before getting a table. The crowd itself gave me a sense of how popular this place is among seafood lovers.

I ordered the Chicken Masala Thali and Crab Masala with Rice Bhakri. The Chicken Masala Thali came with Chicken Gravy, Chicken Rassa, Rice, Bhakri, Sol Kadi, and Salad. The Chicken Gravy had a rich flavour that reminded me of coastal Goan cooking. It had depth, warmth, and a balance of spice. The Chicken Rassa was light and paired beautifully with rice. The Sol Kadi worked as a refreshing sip after the gravies.

The Crab Masala was the highlight of the meal. The crab meat was fresh and sweet. The masala was layered with flavour and had the right amount of spice. The meat absorbed the masala so well that every bite felt satisfying. The staff even help you break the crab if needed, which makes it easier to enjoy. The Rice Bhakri was soft and thick. It soaked up the masala and gravies perfectly.

To finish, I ordered the Caramel Custard. It was smooth, light, and mildly sweet. It balanced the spice of the seafood dishes.

Gomantak is a family-style restaurant that focuses on good food rather than frills. The service was courteous and attentive. The prices are fair for the portions and quality. It is a reliable place in Dadar if you are looking for seafood that feels authentic and comforting.

Ratings:
Quality – 4/5
Quantity – 4.1/5
Service – 4/5
Price – ₹800 for 2 people

For more food experiences, follow @chefvaidehipathare on Instagram!

Restaurant Review: Super Anna Spot, Sion

Just visited the newly opened Coconut lunch home,Super Anna Spot in Sion, and it’s a hidden gem for lovers of Mangalorean cuisine. The standout for me was the benne dosa—soft, rich, and buttery, with that perfect golden crisp that melts in your mouth. It had that authentic South Indian street-style flavor which immediately transported me to Karnataka.

I also tried the chicken green masala, which paired beautifully with both neer dosa and cheese garlic naan. The curry was flavorful, slightly spicy, and had just the right amount of heat to awaken your taste buds without overwhelming them. The kori roti chicken was another hit—a traditional delicacy that was well-executed with crunchy roti pieces soaking up the rich, spicy gravy.

What makes this place special is the wide variety of Mangalorean dishes they offer, which you rarely find in the city. The flavors are bold, authentic, and well-balanced. Portions are generous and pricing feels reasonable for the quality and uniqueness of the food.

Definitely worth a visit if you’re looking to explore something beyond the usual. Super Anna Spot brings a true coastal vibe to the heart of Sion. I’ll be going back for more!

featured_reviews.name: Ilina Banerjee
featured_reviews.review_text:
Tandel's Kitchen in Mahim Seafood Plaza is an extraordinary culinary gem where the ladies of the Koli community masterfully prepare some of the best seafood I've ever tasted. Nestled along the scenic Mahim Sea Beach, with a breathtaking view of the Bandra-Worli Sealink and the soothing Arabian Sea breeze, this place offers more than just food—it's an experience.

During my visit, I had the pleasure of trying several dishes, each leaving a lasting impression. The Surmai Fry was nothing short of spectacular. The fish was incredibly fresh, a testament to their daily fishing activities, and it was cooked to perfection with a flavorful blend of spices that brought out the best in the surmai.

The Prawn Fry was another highlight. The prawns had a perfectly crispy outer layer that gave way to tender, juicy insides. The balance of textures and the well-seasoned coating made each bite a delight.

One of the most memorable dishes was the Clams Masala Curry. It was delightfully spicy, striking a perfect balance that kept it exciting without being overwhelming. The curry had a chatpata (tangy and spicy) taste that was utterly addictive. Paired with the extremely soft Bhakri (a type of flatbread), it created a harmonious combination that was both comforting and satisfying.

What sets Tandel's Kitchen apart is not only the freshness of their seafood but also the unique spice mixes they create in-house. These spices, prepared in a homely style, infuse the dishes with flavors that are rich, vibrant, and authentically Koli.

The ambiance of Tandel's Kitchen significantly enhances the dining experience. Enjoying such flavorful seafood while overlooking the serene Arabian Sea and the iconic Bandra-Worli Sealink, all with the cool sea breeze enveloping you, creates a dining atmosphere that is both relaxing and invigorating.

Tandel's Kitchen is a must-visit for anyone seeking an authentic and extraordinary seafood experience in Mumbai. The combination of fresh, expertly cooked seafood, unique and flavorful spices, and a perfect seaside setting makes it a standout destination. Whether you are a local or a visitor, this place promises a meal that you will not forget.

featured_reviews.name: Jyothis Thaliath
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited this place for lunch.  It’s a Marathi-style seafood speciality restaurant that promises authentic coastal flavours.

Ambience:
The outdoor dining area has a lovely rustic vibe, perfect for evenings or cooler days. However, during hot afternoons, it can get quite uncomfortable. There’s also an indoor, air-conditioned section, but the tables are tightly packed and the sofa type seating is bit aged and not very comfortable.

Food:
We tried two thalis — Mutton Thali and Surmai Thali.

The Mutton Thali was the highlight of our meal. The mutton chops were tender, perfectly spiced, and among the best I’ve had in a while. The gravy was rich and flavourful without being overpowering. The marrow-filled bone was a pleasant surprise.

The Surmai Thali, on the other hand, was average. The fish fry portion was large but just okay in taste.

I wouldn’t recommend the Thalis here overall as most of the side dishes were quite oily and didn’t match my palate (though Maharashtrians might enjoy that style).

Thalis are priced on the higher side (₹600–₹1200). While portions are generous enough to share, I’d suggest skipping the Thali and focusing on starters or individual seafood dishes for better value and taste.

We also tried Butter Garlic Prawns, which were disappointing. Also, the prawns added into Thali curries felt out of place. They could consider swapping a few prawn dishes for clams or calamari, which are common in  Malvani cuisine.

Overall:
Don't fall for the social media hype. It's good for a visit if you’re in Aarey and craving for seafood.

Overall, the food wasn’t bad, just pretty underwhelming for the pricing and hype. Maybe Goan flavors are intentionally subtler and my palate leans more towards Konkani/Malvani seafood.

A must-visit landmark for anyone who appreciates quality, tradition, and genuine taste.

featured_reviews.name: Sagar Abichandani
featured_reviews.review_text:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ (4/5)

Ramashray in Matunga is one of those classic South Indian institutions that still feels properly “Bombay” – bustling, no-nonsense and absolutely focused on the food. I dropped in specifically to try their ghee podi Thatte idli and walked out very happy (and very full).

The ghee podi Thatte idli is easily the hero of the menu. The idli itself is thick and soft – that perfect Thatte style – with a beautiful fermented flavour. It comes drenched in ghee, with a generous ring of podi that clings to every bite. The texture, temperature and seasoning were spot on; this is the kind of dish you could reorder without thinking twice.

The pineapple sheera was another standout. Warm, fragrant and not cloyingly sweet, with enough pineapple to cut through the richness of ghee – it felt like a proper old-school dessert, the kind you’d expect from a place that’s been doing this for decades. If you have a sweet tooth, this is non-negotiable.

Where the experience dipped a bit for me was the masala dosa. For a place with Ramashray’s reputation, I expected a benchmark dosa, but it was underwhelming:
•	The dosa was small in size compared to typical Matunga standards.
•	The texture lacked crispness – instead of that satisfying crunch, the dosa kept crumbling even when handled gently, which made it messy and not very enjoyable.
•	The masala itself was decent, but the base failed to carry it.

Service is fast, efficient and very typical of old-school South Indian joints in Mumbai – you’re seated, served and cleared quickly, which works well given the constant rush. Prices are reasonable for the quality, and the overall vibe is nostalgic: crowded, lively, with conversations, steel plates and filter coffee aromas all blending into one.

Overall, Ramashray still deserves its cult status for certain dishes, especially the ghee podi Thatte idli and pineapple sheera, which I would come back for in a heartbeat. I’m giving it 4 stars only because the masala dosa – usually the litmus test at a South Indian eatery – fell short on texture and portion size. Fix that, and this would easily be a 5-star experience.

I usually write reviews when I truly like a place, but I felt the need to share this experience because my stomach was upset after eating here, which is concerning.

I visited this restaurant expecting authentic Ratnagiri/Konkan food, especially given the name and the 4-star rating. Unfortunately, the food did not meet those expectations at all.

I ordered a fish thali, but there was nothing about it that reflected true Konkan or Ratnagiri cuisine. The fish fry was bland, not properly marinated, and lacked basic flavor. I had to add salt, pepper, and lime myself just to make it edible. Authentic Konkan fish fry is known for its seasoning and marinade, which was completely missing here.

The fish curry was a simple onion-based gravy with no depth—no kokum, no tamarind, no spice, and not even the correct color of a traditional fish curry. The thali included bhakri, rice, fish fry, fish curry, sol curry, and a dry fish preparation. Except for the dry item, nothing tasted authentic or satisfying.

I also ordered chicken sukka, which is supposed to be dry and at least mildly spicy. What was served was more like a regular chicken curry with gravy, not dry at all, and completely lacking spice and flavor. It did not resemble chicken sukka in any way.

I had high expectations, but the food was nowhere near what one would expect from a place claiming to serve Ratnagiri or Konkan cuisine. This food does not represent Konkan food, not even remotely.

Overall, a very disappointing experience, and due to both the quality of the food and the health issue afterward, I would not recommend this restaurant.

customer_updates.text:
A Disappointing Thaali Experience

My recent visit to this restaurant left much to be desired, particularly concerning their thaali offerings. While some aspects were tolerable, several critical flaws made for a truly underwhelming experience.

1) Quantity Concerns
Practically all thaali options severely lack in quantity. What's served feels more like an appetizer than a substantial meal. Thaalis, if nothing else, should be known for their generous portions. The amount we received made us question if it was truly a thaali or merely a half-thaali (even though we didn't order the latter).

2) Quality and Ambiance
I won't heavily critique the quality of the food, as it wasn't outright bad, but let's just say it wholeheartedly embraces mediocrity.
As for the ambiance, the place tries too hard to mimic the rustic vibe of a Konkani Waada but fails miserably. Instead, it now resembles a poorly lit, questionable restaurant that seems better suited for unsavory characters.

3) Service Shortcomings
Perhaps it was an isolated incident, but the server assigned to our table struggled to speak clearly. We could barely hear him, making it impossible to communicate or inquire about the dishes. This wasn't a language barrier; it simply seemed he was disengaged from his job.
Furthermore, no server approached us to ask if we needed anything. It made us wonder if we were paying customers or if they were doing us a charity by feeding us for free.

4) Unacceptable Thaali Details
The thaali lacks essential condiments. The onions served on the side were poorly prepared, coming as huge, unappetizing chunks in a tiny bowl. Ideally, onion rings would be provided for ease of picking.

The charges for the thaali are absurdly high for the meager amount provided. I've attached a picture of the pomfret thaali; notice the fish was chopped instead of being served whole. What kind of thaali serves fish like this? It's as if they don't differentiate between a fish thaali and a fish starter, providing the same portion for both.

We were charged over ₹1000 for this thaali. I know at least 25 other places that offer a far better value pomfret thaali for around ₹800. I may sound like a broken record, but thaalis are supposed to be this place's unique selling point. Getting so many things wrong with them makes me question if they truly thought things through when they decided to feature thaalis prominently on their menu.

5) Staff Demeanor
The staff and management exude fake politeness. It's as if they resent working there or are simply disengaged.
A Personal Disappointment
To be fair, this next point is a bit personal and may not apply to everyone, but it's worth mentioning. Tonight was a special occasion for me (a Kelvan, a Marathi get-together for a groom-to-be). My friends brought a Baskin Robbins cake, and we simply asked if we could cut it there after our meal – we didn't ask them to prepare it. They refused us permission. How can a place charge so much per thaali and then deny customers the chance to acknowledge a special day? It felt as though this establishment actively discourages celebrations. What kind of business drives away potential sales by being unaccommodating to pre- and post-celebration arrangements?

6) Uncomfortable Seating
Finally, the seating arrangement was slightly uncomfortable. The tables were a bit too large, the chairs didn't prioritize comfort, and the sofas attached to the walls were old and thus uncomfortable.

featured_reviews.name: tejas thorat
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently had the privilege of dining at The Maratha Kitchen, courtesy of our boss, who treated our team to a lunch outing. What started as a casual team lunch quickly turned into one of the most memorable Maharashtrian dining experiences I have had in recent times.

As someone from the hospitality industry and a passionate food enthusiast, I can confidently say that The Maratha Kitchen stands apart for its authenticity, consistency, and unwavering commitment to quality. Much of the credit goes to owner Abhishek Tulaskar, a passionate hotelier with extensive industry experience. His understanding of food, sourcing, and guest experience is evident in every aspect of the restaurant.

One thing that immediately impressed me was Abhishek's uncompromising approach towards the quality of mutton served. He is extremely selective about sourcing and accepts nothing short of the best. In an era where portion sizes are often shrinking, The Maratha Kitchen takes a refreshingly generous approach. Almost every mutton entrée contains nearly a quarter kilogram of mutton, ensuring diners receive both exceptional quality and outstanding value.

Our group of six largely opted for the Maratha Mutton Thali and Kolhapuri Mutton Thali, accompanied by Bombil Rawa Fry and Prawn Rawa Fry, Mutton kharda, Prawn agri masala.

The thalis are thoughtfully curated and offer a complete Maharashtrian culinary experience. Each thali includes Mutton Sukka, Mutton Rassa, Alni Rassa, Solkadhi, fragrant Indrayani Rice, and a choice between traditional Jowar Bhakri or rice bhakri and koshimbir.

The waiting time for the thalis was approximately 20-25 minutes, but the freshness and quality of preparation made the wait completely worthwhile.

The Bombil Rawa Fry deserves special mention. The bombil was expertly flattened, marinated beautifully, coated with rawa, and fried until perfectly crisp while retaining its delicate texture. The Prawn Rawa Fry was equally impressive, fresh, juicy, and packed with flavour.

Coming to the star attraction, the mutton.

The Mutton Sukka was robust and flavourful, showcasing a perfect balance of spices while allowing the quality of the meat to shine through. The Mutton Rassa was rich, aromatic, and deeply satisfying. However, the true hero of the meal was undoubtedly the Alni Rassa. Often overshadowed by its spicier counterparts, this version was exceptional. Light yet intensely flavourful, it carried the essence of slow-cooked mutton stock and delivered remarkable depth and comfort with every spoonful.

The restaurant's Tambda Rassa and Pandhra Rassa are beautifully balanced. They provide enough spice and richness to excite the palate without overwhelming the natural flavour of the meat.

If there is one dish that every diner must order, it is unquestionably the Mutton Kharda.

In my opinion, it is one of the finest versions available in the city today. Despite being one of the simplest preparations on the menu, it was easily the most memorable dish of the afternoon. Tender pieces of mutton are slow-cooked in ghee and paired with freshly pounded green chilli thecha and turmeric. The meat is so tender that it effortlessly falls off the bone. The richness of the ghee beautifully complements the sharp heat of the chillies, creating a dish that is rustic, honest, and incredibly flavourful. Sometimes the simplest recipes produce the most unforgettable results, and this dish is proof of that.

Another standout was the Agri Prawns, tossed in a bold Agri-style masala and cooked with the shells intact to preserve maximum flavour. Every bite delivered an authentic coastal character that seafood lovers will appreciate.

After such a hearty and spice-forward meal, the desserts provided the perfect conclusion. The Peru Ice Cream was refreshing and unique, while the Narali Bhat Ice Cream brilliantly captured the essence of the traditional Maharashtrian sweet dish in frozen form. Both desserts acted as excellent palate cleansers and a fitting finale to the meal.

Rating: 4.8/5

Hits and misses at this Mangalorean spot:

​I visited The Fisherman’s Kitchen on a Friday evening with high expectations, given the name and the positive reviews. While the atmosphere is family-friendly and the location is convenient (right below Bangur Nagar Metro with valet parking), the food was a mixed bag.
​The Standouts: The Pomfret in Banana Leaf was easily the highlight—the fish was incredibly fresh and perfectly cooked (4.5/5). Pairing the remaining gravy with Neer Dosa was the best part of the meal.
​The Letdowns: Unfortunately, the Prawns Tandoori didn't taste fresh (2.5/5), and the Crab Soup was watery with very little meat. The Kadipatta Chicken was also quite average; the chicken felt a bit tough and lacked that punchy Mangalorean flavor I was looking for.
​The Verdict:
​Ambience & Service: 3.5/5
​Alcohol Variety: 4/5
Food: 3/5
​Value for Money: 3/5
It’s a decent place for a family outing, and perhaps I caught them on an off-night, but for a seafood specialty restaurant, I expected more consistency in freshness.

It's the kind of place you visit when you crave authentic, home-style seafood and fiery curries.
The highlight here is, without a doubt, the seafood. The fish is always incredibly fresh—a mandatory requirement for any great coastal establishment. I highly recommend starting with the Bombil Fry (Bombay Duck) or the Surmai Fry. The coating is perfectly crisp, and the marinade is a flawless blend of chili, turmeric, and spice. For the main course, the Prawn Curry Thali is a masterpiece; rich, coconut-based gravy that pairs perfectly with the soft, fluffy Vade (puri made from rice and lentil flour). If you prefer meat, the Chicken Malvani Thali is equally robust and satisfying.
Beyond the main courses, don't miss out on the incredible Solkadhi. This kokam-based digestive drink is creamy, tangy, and absolutely essential for cooling the palate after the spicy Konkani flavors. It’s one of the best I've had outside of a Konkani home.
The ambiance is simple, clean, and unpretentious, allowing the focus to remain solely on the food, as it should be. The staff is warm, helpful, and eager to offer recommendations, making the entire dining experience feel incredibly homely. If you love coastal flavors, fresh fish, and authentic Malvani spices, Konkan Swad is a must-visit destination in Jogeshwari. Highly, highly recommended!

featured_reviews.name: Yogita Uchil
featured_reviews.review_text:
Whenever I’m in a new city, I make it a point to explore its traditional flavors. In Mumbai, Malvani food is always on my list. Since I was staying near Malad West, I decided to try Surmai, a Malvani/Mangalorean restaurant.
We ordered quite a few dishes, and while there were some good ones, the experience was mixed overall. Unfortunately, the signature dishes were a letdown. The fish curry in the thali was bland, lacking any real flavor, and the fish itself seemed like old stock. The bangda/mackerel fry was also disappointing, with fish that tasted frozen and not fresh.
On the brighter side, the clam sukka and prawn rava fry were enjoyable and definitely stood out. The sol kadhi, however, was more about color than taste and lacked the authentic punch.
I wish the restaurant paid more attention to freshness and flavor, especially in their star dishes, because Malvani food deserves much better representation.
